instructions:
## Research objective

Your goal is to design reasoning and prompt engineering techniques to maximize accuracy for measuring peer-review quality signals and evaluating a two-stage, bi-directional author-feedback review and reviewer reward system in AI conferences.

## Plan Formulation

- Reproduce and extend three empirical components from the paper: (A) ICLR keyword dynamics (2018–2025), (B) LLM-assisted typo-rate trends in ICLR peer reviews (2017–2024+), (C) cross-venue reviewer reward/recognition audit (2020–2025).
- Design a pilot evaluation of the two-stage, bi-directional review workflow with author feedback and LLM-generated reference reviews: simulate at scale and, if feasible, run a small real-user study or sandbox trial on public preprints.
- Develop strict-output LLM prompts and schemas for: (1) typo detection under math-aware constraints, (2) section-1 review generation (summary/strengths/questions), (3) section-2 review generation (weaknesses/rating), (4) author feedback scoring rubrics, (5) optional LLM-likeness similarity checks.
- Define quantitative metrics: errors per 1,000 words; proportion of error-free reviews; year-over-year trends; top-20 keyword churn; reviewer badge thresholds (top 10%/30%); reviewer impact score formulations; simulated retaliation bias reduction under two-stage release.
- Pre-register core hypotheses: H1 typo rates decline over years; H2 two-stage release reduces retaliatory author scoring; H3 badge thresholds are stable with sufficient author-feedback samples; H4 LLM reference reviews deter low-effort LLM-only human reviews.
- Set constraints: adhere to OpenReview TOS; only use public data; minimize potential re-identification; avoid collecting sensitive metadata beyond what is public.
- Keep system prompts consistent and minimal, emphasizing JSON-only outputs for machine parsing; avoid free-form chain-of-thought and instead request short, structured rationales when needed.
- Target rapid first-pass replication; iterate with ablations (different LLMs, detectors, math filters). Do not over-plan; ship an initial end-to-end pipeline quickly.

## Data Preparation

- OpenReview ingestion (ICLR 2017–2025): download submissions, decisions, reviewer comments, ratings, timestamps, and author-provided keywords; exclude desk-rejected papers for keyword analysis per the paper.
- Normalization for reviews: remove or mask LaTeX math ($...$, $$...$$), code blocks, and inline formulas; normalize whitespace; segment reviews into ≤2,000 token chunks for LLM calls; record original length in words.
- Typo-detection dataset: for each review and chunk, create inputs to the typo detector; store raw model JSON outputs; merge chunk-level results; compute review-level error counts and types (typo/spell/plural).
- Build a math-aware ignore list and tokenization rules to reduce false positives; validate on a hand-labeled sample of 200 review snippets for quality control.
- Keyword dataset: lowercase keywords; trim punctuation; map abbreviations to canonical forms (e.g., nlp→natural language processing; gnn→graph neural network); maintain a transparent mapping table in a YAML file with version control.
- Compute keyword frequencies per year; select top-20 annually; compute entry/exit churn and overlaps; store per-year CSVs and a consolidated parquet.
- Reviewer reward audit dataset (2020–2025): define schema venue, year, RHF_present(bool), in_kind_comp(bool), notes(url/evidence); populate by scraping official conference sites and CfR pages; store as CSV with citation links; record scrape date.
- LLM reference reviews dataset: for a sample of public preprints (e.g., recent arXiv ML papers), extract title/abstract/method and generate section-1 and section-2 LLM reviews; store with prompt/version/model/temperature seeds.
- Author feedback rubric: define JSON schema with numeric scales for comprehension and question constructiveness (e.g., 1–5), plus optional free-text justification (max 300 chars); store as a form template.
- Ethics and privacy: maintain a data dictionary; exclude reviewer identities where not public; do not attempt de-anonymization; document TOS compliance; include a risk register (e.g., misclassification harms, detector bias).

## Running Experiments

- Environment: Python 3.11; packages openreview-py, pandas, numpy, scipy, seaborn, matplotlib/plotnine, scikit-learn, statsmodels, pydantic, tiktoken, httpx/requests, beautifulsoup4; LLM SDKs for selected models.
- OpenReview fetch: respect rate limits (sleep/backoff); paginate; cache JSON responses locally; maintain deterministic snapshots via timestamped dumps.
- Typo detection with LLM: temperature=0, top_p=1; strict JSON schema with fields original_word, correction, error_type in an array; instruct model to ignore math and non-spelling issues; chunk long reviews; parallelize with bounded concurrency; cache results.
- Rule-based baseline: run a math-aware pipeline (strip LaTeX; wordlist checker such as wordfreq+pyspellchecker or language-tool with custom dictionary); compute errors per 1,000 words; compare with LLM outputs; report Cohen’s kappa and Bland–Altman plots.
- Metrics: per-year mean errors/1k words, median, IQR; fraction of error-free reviews; robust trend via Theil–Sen and Mann–Kendall; sensitivity to chunk size and math-filter settings; bootstrap CIs.
- Keyword analysis: compute top-20 per year; churn (entered/dropped); visualize area charts and chord/flow of keywords; replicate table structure from Appendix A; verify with manual spot checks.
- Reviewer reward audit: programmatically verify URLs; update structured table; compute counts by year; reproduce summary tallies similar to Appendix C.
- Two-stage workflow simulation: create an agent-based model of papers, reviewers, and authors; include parameters for author-outcome bias (authors rate reviews higher when accepted), elongated-review bias (length inflates perceived quality), and retaliation probability; compare one-shot vs two-stage release (section-1 rated before weaknesses/ratings revealed).
- Retaliation mitigation experiment: in simulation, lock author feedback after section-1; measure reduction in bias of feedback relative to final accept/reject; vary safeguards (length caps on section-1; mandatory justification for low scores; optional LLM-reference visibility).
- LLM reference review deterrence: for each paper, generate section-1 LLM review; compute semantic similarity (e.g., sentence-BERT) between human reviews and LLM reference; flag very high similarity with low specificity language; track false positives via manual audit on a small sample.
- Badge threshold robustness: simulate distribution of author feedback per reviewer across multiple assignments; estimate how many reviews are needed for stable top 10%/30% identification (power curves); evaluate fairness (e.g., differences by reviewer seniority proxies if available).
- Reviewer impact score prototype: define formula variants (e.g., sum over reviewed papers of min(1, weight)*log(1+citations at 2 years)); test on public citation APIs (OpenAlex/Crossref) for a subset; examine correlation with badge status and assignment difficulty.
- Ablations: swap LLMs for typo detection (e.g., Gemini, GPT, Claude) and compare; run with and without math stripping; evaluate JSON function-calling vs text prompting; vary temperature and nucleus sampling.
- Reproducibility: log seeds, model versions, prompts, and hyperparameters; use a local SQLite/duckdb for experiment tracking; persist all intermediate artifacts; generate a Makefile or workflow for end-to-end runs.

## Results Interpretation

- Report year-over-year typo trends with effect sizes, CIs, and p-values; contextualize declines with confounders (spell-check prevalence, reviewer composition changes, review length).
- Discuss agreement and divergences between LLM-based and rule-based typo detectors; analyze systematic biases (technical terms, names, UK/US variants); include error-type distributions.
- Summarize keyword churn: which topics rise/fall; relate to field dynamics; check for sensitivity to canonicalization rules; highlight years with largest shifts.
- Synthesize reviewer reward audit: visibility of RHF and compensation over time; identify venues improving incentives; note gaps and inconsistencies.
- Two-stage simulation outcomes: quantify reduction in author-outcome bias and retaliation compared to baseline; show sensitivity to section-1 length caps and mandatory justifications; discuss trade-offs (reviewer effort, time).
- Assess LLM reference deterrence: did similarity-based flags correlate with superficiality metrics without over-flagging substantive human reviews? quantify precision/recall on audited samples.
- Badge thresholds and impact score: assess stability, fairness, and susceptibility to gaming; recommend minimum number of reviews for eligibility; propose safeguards (e.g., meta-review oversight, anomaly detection).
- Limitations: public data scope; simulation assumptions; detector fallibility; ethical considerations; external validity across venues.
- Actionable recommendations for conferences and OpenReview: phased pilots, minimal UI changes for two-stage release, public badges with standardized schema, opt-in reviewer activity tracking.

## Report Writing

- Create a structured paper with sections: Background and Motivation; Data and Methods (OpenReview pipelines, prompts, detectors); Results (typo trends, keywords, reward audit); Two-Stage Simulation; Badge/Impact Metrics; Limitations and Ethics; Recommendations.
- Include appendices with: prompt templates; canonicalization mapping table; audit code for website scraping; full statistical tables; sensitivity analyses; detailed simulation parameters.
- Provide clear figures: trend lines with CIs for typo metrics; stacked area plots for keywords; heatmaps for churn; tables summarizing RHF/compensation by venue/year; simulation outcome plots.
- Document all prompts, model versions, and settings; provide exact JSON schemas; share reproducible scripts and environment files; deposit data snapshots where licenses allow.
- Conclude with a practical rollout plan for a pilot two-stage review and badge system, including metrics for success, required platform changes, and a timeline for evaluation.
